findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 fetches only 50 public group members without pagination or subsequent fetches, making remaining members inaccessible.
app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, overcounting pages for exact multiples of the limit and enabling navigation to an empty page.
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 routes existing PATCH membership requests to update, which ignores changes and returns success without updating membership.
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 sets visible to false when the parameter is absent, unexpectedly hiding groups during PATCH membership requests.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 fetches only 50 public group members without pagination or subsequent fetches, making remaining members inaccessible.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for group-members.js.es6, the setupController calls model.findMembers() which fetches members with a default limit of 50 (defined in group.js). However, examining the template group/members.hbs, it iterates over 'members' but there's no pagination UI shown in this template for the public group members view. The admin view (admin/templates/group.hbs) has pagination controls with 'previous' and 'next' actions, but the public group members template doesn't have these controls. This means public group members beyond the first 50 would be inaccessible. The finding correctly identifies that only 50 members are fetched without pagination for the public view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 routes existing PATCH membership requests to update, which ignores changes and returns success without updating membership.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the update method in groups_controller.rb was changed. The old code had separate handling for PATCH vs PUT requests (update_patch vs update_put methods). The new update method only handles basic group properties (alias_level, visible, name) and does NOT handle membership changes at all. The old update_patch method that handled 'changes' parameter with 'add' and 'delete' arrays for membership was removed. However, the routes.rb diff shows that membership operations are now handled by separate endpoints: 'delete members => groups#remove_member' and 'put members => groups#add_members'. So PATCH requests to the main update endpoint would now go to the new update method which doesn't handle membership - but this is intentional as membership is now managed through dedicated endpoints. The finding claims line 34 routes PATCH to update, but looking at the new code structure, membership is handled by add_members and remove_member actions. The old PATCH behavior for membership changes was intentionally removed and replaced with dedicated endpoints. This is a design change, not a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 sets visible to false when the parameter is absent, unexpectedly hiding groups during PATCH membership requests.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the update method in groups_controller.rb sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` on line 34. This means if the visible parameter is absent or any value other than the string 'true', visible will be set to false. However, examining the diff more carefully, the old code also had `group.visible = payload[:visible] == "true"` which had the same behavior. The finding claims this is problematic for 'PATCH membership requests', but the diff shows the PATCH-style update_patch method was removed entirely - the new code only has add_members and remove_member methods which don't touch the visible property at all. The update method is now only called for PUT requests to update group settings, not for membership changes. So the concern about membership requests affecting visibility is not valid in the new code structure.
